5975-thomas-wingfold-curate-v3:
George MacDonald opens the third volume after the sermon, as the preacher's emotion clears and single faces dawn again on his sight. Mr. Drew's head is down, and old trade practices once counted honest now seem hateful to him, with their memory intolerable. He knows he shrank from the light in taking such gains.

The volume follows his effort to banish those mean ways from his business, even as they remain a painful presence. It carries the curate's story toward reckoning, where conscience presses harder than comfort and a man's past dealings must be faced.
frus-1872p2v3:
Arguments fill Volume III of the Geneva arbitration papers. The American argument leads, delivered June 15, 1872. It frames the legal issue in plain terms. A state suppressing revolt, it says, exercises belligerent powers. Other powers must not intervene under neutrality's name. Britain's argument answers with its own summary. It ties every loss to a specific failure of duty.

Supplementary statements from both sides close the volume. Counsel argue over how damages should be measured. A gross sum, the British side insists, cannot float free of proof. The papers are dense with legal reasoning. They also carry the war's full grievance in formal dress. Readers see international law being made. The tribunal's task narrows to ships and duties.
frus-1873p2v3:
This volume reports the American and British Joint Claims Commission. Robert Hale, the American agent, writes the main report. The commission judged citizens' claims against both governments. Its basis was the twelfth article of the 1871 treaty. A general appendix prints how the settlement was built. Fish and Sir Edward Thornton exchange the first letters. Commissioners receive appointments and instructions.

A confidential memorandum briefs the American side. It covers the fisheries and the St. Lawrence navigation. Canada trade and the San Juan boundary appear. Rebel cruiser claims get their own heading. Protocols record the Washington conferences of early 1871. One paper recalls Pickett's landing on San Juan in 1859. The volume documents diplomacy by commission. Claims became a system here.
thomas-wingfold-curate-v3:
Volume three of George MacDonald's Thomas Wingfold, Curate opens after a sermon in the Abbey Church at Olaston. Mr. Drew sits with his head down, weeping unnoticed. Business practices he once counted honest now look hateful when judged by a divine standard for merchants.

He longs for final deliverance from advantages that shrank from the light, even when he hardly knew their full nature. Wingfold preached in general terms, yet one hearer feels personally convicted. Readers get the closing volume of a religious novel about conscience, trade, and a curate whose sermons remake the people who hear them.
